coalbiomassboiler_over_citation.finding: coalbiomassboiler.com is cited 7 times across the two files (VC source 2, VC source 4, PP5.2 sources 1 and 2, PP5.2 source 6, PP5.4 source 1, PP5.3 source 2). Under the same-publisher-family rule all 7 citations count as ONE unique source. This single vendor blog is the sole backing for: (a) all spare-parts lead times (PP5.4's core quantitative claim), (b) all retrofit capex figures (PP5.2's core cost claim including the $300K–$1.2M and 15–30% CAPEX addition cited in the task brief), and (c) Malaysia EQA 2014 stack limits. The concentration of critical claims on one vendor blog is the most significant source quality failure in this stage.

lautan_air_over_citation.finding: beta.co.id and lautanairindonesia.com are both Lautan Air Indonesia content properties. Collectively cited 6+ times. This single vendor's marketing blog is the sole backing for: (a) RM 228K–630K/hr downtime cost (PP5.1 and PP5.4 cost anchors), (b) blowdown rate 10–20% vs. optimal <1% (PP5.3), (c) biomass fuel consumption figures used in the efficiency penalty arithmetic. The 20–25% scale efficiency loss is cross-validated by the National Board, but all dollar-quantified downstream calculations use Lautan Air arithmetic only.

SSI_2025_source_assessment.finding: PP5.5 raises Malaysia's OSH SSI Regulations 2025 as a significant compliance cliff. The claim is supported by three independent secondary-trade sources (Lexology, Skrine Advocates & Solicitors, Advanced HSE Solutions). Skrine is a reputable Malaysian law firm whose client alert directly summarizes the regulation. No official DOSH gazette, the PUA 99 text, or official DOSH portal page is cited. This is the most critical gap: the regulation exists and the Skrine alert is credible but the primary official document would upgrade this from Medium to High. The task brief asked specifically whether this was 'primary-sourced (gazette, DOSH, Lexology/Skrine analysis)' — the answer is: Skrine analysis YES (secondary_trade from a reputable legal firm), DOSH gazette NO, primary DOSH portal NO.
SSI_2025_source_assessment.recommendation: Search DOSH Malaysia official website for OSH (Special Scheme of Inspection) Regulations 2025 PUA text; search MyGov portal for P.U.(A) number; search Bernama or parliamentary records for gazette date.

water_treatment_scale_efficiency_loss.finding: The '20–25% efficiency loss from 1/8 inch scale' claim appears in VC5-act3-1 and PP5.3-cost-1 and PP5.3-freq-2. It IS cross-validated: the National Board of Boiler and Pressure Vessel Inspectors (nationalboard.org — primary_association) independently confirms the 20–25% figure. This is one of the few well-evidenced quantitative claims in the stage. Medium confidence is appropriate. It is not Low.
water_treatment_scale_efficiency_loss.verdict: Cross-validated. Medium confidence. No deep research priority needed for this specific sub-claim.

ILO_inspector_ratio_1_57000.finding: The ILO 1:57,000 inspector ratio for Indonesia is sourced from ilo.org/media/425611/download (ILO factsheet) AND corroborated by the Kemnaker OSH Profile 2022 (satudata.kemnaker.go.id) cited as source 7 in PP5.1. The ILO factsheet is primary_multilateral. Kemnaker OSH Profile is a primary_ministry document from the Ministry of Manpower. These are two independent primary sources. The inspector ratio claim is the best-sourced quantitative claim in the stage.
ILO_inspector_ratio_1_57000.verdict: ILO 1:57,000 ratio: High confidence (two independent primary sources). The 4,068 Kelas I operator count is from 2017 data within the Kemnaker profile — stale but primary-sourced.

retrofit_cost_PP5.2_assessment.finding: The task brief specifically asks about '$100K–$1.2M for 3–5 t/h systems.' The $300K–$1.2M total system figure and the $100K–$500K baghouse component both trace exclusively to coalbiomassboiler.com (two pages from same domain). No primary source, industry association report, or independent engineering cost study is cited. This is the single most important weak claim for deep research: it is the cost anchor for the entire PP5.2 argument and rests on a single vendor blog.
retrofit_cost_PP5.2_assessment.verdict: Low confidence. Single vendor blog source. Deep research priority: HIGH.

lead_time_assessment_6_12_week_tubes.finding: The '6–12 week tube bundle' and '8–14 week boiler shell' lead times are sourced exclusively from coalbiomassboiler.com/industrial-boiler-spare-parts-delivery/. No OEM direct quotation, shipping data, or independent logistics study is cited. Single vendor blog source.
lead_time_assessment_6_12_week_tubes.verdict: Low confidence. Deep research priority: HIGH.

weak_claims_to_deep_research.claim_text: Total installed emissions control system for 3–5 t/h boiler $300K–$1.2M; compliance costs add 15–30% to CAPEX; baghouse $100K–$500K, scrubber $150K–$750K, CEMS $40K–$120K
weak_claims_to_deep_research.issue: Both sources are the same vendor blog domain. The $300K–$1.2M range is the primary cost anchor for PP5.2 — if this is inflated or deflated, the entire retrofit bifurcation argument collapses. No engineering cost data, no equipment manufacturer price list, no EPC project cost disclosure.
weak_claims_to_deep_research.suggested_action: Search: (1) VIRIDIS Engineering Malaysia or Arrow Energy Thailand for published ESP/baghouse case studies with cost disclosure; (2) IEA or IRENA biomass energy cost reports for SEA air pollution control costs; (3) World Bank ESMAP reports on industrial emissions control costs in Indonesia/Malaysia; (4) ADB project documents for biomass power/industrial energy projects that include APC system cost breakdowns; (5) Indonesian or Malaysian EPC project cost audits filed with KLHK or DOE under CEMS installation requirements

weak_claims_to_deep_research.claim_text: Tube bundles 6–12 weeks lead time; boiler shells 8–14 weeks from OEM factory
weak_claims_to_deep_research.issue: This is the structural claim that makes PP5.4 commercially urgent: if parts lead times are actually 2–4 weeks (as may be the case with bonded warehouse distributors in Singapore or Malaysia), the pain point severity diminishes substantially. The only source is a vendor blog with commercial interest in making lead times sound long (to sell stocked inventory). No shipping data, OEM order confirmation, or parts distributor interview cited.
weak_claims_to_deep_research.suggested_action: Search: (1) Direct request to Inmech Malaysia or PT Atmindo — what is actual current lead time for SA-210 replacement tube bundle for a 10 t/h Thermax or ZBG boiler? (2) Singapore bonded warehouse industrial parts distributor lead times; (3) ZBG, Thermax, or EPCB official after-sales parts catalogue lead time statements; (4) PT Atmindo annual report or investor communications for parts supply discussion

weak_claims_to_deep_research.claim_text: Palm oil mill boiler downtime costs RM 228,000–630,000 per hour in lost CPO throughput
weak_claims_to_deep_research.issue: This figure is the highest-stakes cost claim in the entire stage. It anchors PP5.1 (compliance gap cost), PP5.3 (tube failure cost), and PP5.4 (forced outage during parts wait). The range implies a palm oil mill processes RM 228K–630K/hr of fresh fruit bunches, which is a figure only achievable by large-capacity mills (60–90 t FFB/hr). The source is a single Lautan Air Indonesia marketing article. No MPOB statistics, CPO price data model, or mill throughput engineering calculation is cited. Any reader challenging this figure would question the magnitude of pain across three pain points simultaneously.
weak_claims_to_deep_research.suggested_action: Search: (1) MPOB Annual Statistics 2024 for average CPO mill throughput and CPO selling price to back-calculate shutdown cost per hour; (2) Malaysia Palm Oil Board economic studies or consultant reports on palm oil mill downtime costs; (3) Published insurance actuarial data on business interruption claims for Malaysian palm oil mills from Allianz or Chubb Malaysia; (4) GAPKI Indonesia palm oil statistics for FFB processing rates at medium/large mills

weak_claims_to_deep_research.claim_text: Malaysia OSH SSI Regulations 2025 effective January 21, 2025; CF valid up to 60 months for qualifying facilities
weak_claims_to_deep_research.issue: Three secondary-trade sources from different credible organizations. The Skrine alert is particularly credible (Malaysian law firm). However, the primary official document (DOSH Malaysia gazette, PUA 99 text, official DOSH portal page for SSI Regulations) is not cited. For a 'compliance cliff' claim that anchors PP5.5 and is flagged as a novel finding, the absence of the primary official document limits the claim to Medium and leaves the specific terms (60-month maximum, Class A/B structure) unvalidated at primary level.
weak_claims_to_deep_research.suggested_action: Search: (1) DOSH Malaysia official website (dosh.gov.my) for OSH (Special Scheme of Inspection) Regulations 2025 — look for P.U.(A) gazette reference; (2) Malaysian Attorney General's Chambers e-legislation portal for the PUA 99 text; (3) MPKKP or NIOSH Malaysia for SSI implementation guidance; (4) Confirm whether 'Class A (120 months) and Class B (180 months) for Steam Boilers' referenced in Advanced HSE Solutions is from the same regulation or a different instrument

weak_claims_to_deep_research.claim_text: Indonesia: 1,470 labor inspectors, 1:57,000 ratio; boiler Kelas I operator pool 4,068 persons (2017)
weak_claims_to_deep_research.current_score: High (inspector ratio) / Low (operator count — stale 2017 data)
weak_claims_to_deep_research.issue: The inspector ratio is well-sourced (ILO + Kemnaker = two primaries). The 4,068 Kelas I operator count is stale (2017). This is the denominator for the critical 'fewer than 1 certified operator per boiler' calculation that anchors PP5.1's severity. If the operator count has grown since 2017 (e.g., to 8,000+), the apparent scarcity ratio changes materially.
weak_claims_to_deep_research.suggested_action: Search: (1) Kemnaker satudata.kemnaker.go.id for most recent Kelas I and II operator certification statistics (2022–2025); (2) BPS Indonesia manpower statistics for 'tenaga teknik khusus boiler'; (3) ILO Indonesia OSH programme 2024–2029 documentation for any updated operator certification statistics

weak_claims_to_deep_research.claim_text: Indonesia engineer-per-million ratio 2,671 vs. Malaysia 3,333, Thailand 4,121 (PwC 2017)
weak_claims_to_deep_research.issue: PwC Indonesia 2017 — 9 years old. This is the comparative structural claim about engineering workforce scarcity. Given rapid growth in university engineering enrollment in Indonesia 2017–2025, the figure may significantly understate current capacity. Any investor would immediately question a 9-year-old PwC slide.
weak_claims_to_deep_research.suggested_action: Search: (1) BPS Indonesia 'jumlah insinyur per juta penduduk 2022 2023 2024'; (2) World Bank Human Capital Report 2023 for Indonesia engineering workforce; (3) OECD/ADB skill gap reports for Southeast Asia technical workforce 2022–2025; (4) Ministry of Education Indonesia (Kemendikbud) engineering graduate output statistics

weak_claims_to_deep_research.claim_text: China 71% of Indonesia HS 8402 boiler import value ($737M) in 2023
weak_claims_to_deep_research.issue: TrendEconomy is a secondary data aggregator. The underlying data would be from BPS Indonesia or UN Comtrade (both primary). The HS 8402 figure anchors the claim about Chinese OEM dominance driving the parts scarcity problem. A BPS primary citation would upgrade this to Medium.
weak_claims_to_deep_research.suggested_action: Search: (1) BPS Indonesia external trade statistics HS 8402 (boilers) 2023 — bps.go.id; (2) UN Comtrade database for Indonesia HS 8402 imports 2023; (3) Confirm whether HS 8402 captures solid-fuel package boilers or is dominated by power plant boilers

gate_reasoning: Stage 5 scores 66 Low out of 95 total claims (69.5% Low), placing it just below the 70% automatic FAIL threshold applied to Stage 3. However, four structural source quality problems require flagging before this stage is treated as ready for synthesis. First, coalbiomassboiler.com is cited seven times but counts as one source; it is the sole backing for the entire PP5.2 retrofit cost argument ($300K–$1.2M, 15–30% CAPEX addition) and the entire PP5.4 spare-parts lead time argument (6–14 weeks). Both are critical quantitative anchors for major pain points, and both are from a single vendor blog with commercial interest in the subject. Second, the RM 228K–630K/hr downtime figure — which cascades through three pain points (PP5.1, PP5.3, PP5.4) as the primary cost-severity anchor — comes from a single Lautan Air Indonesia marketing article. These two vendor-blog dependencies represent the most material source quality risk in this stage. Third, the Malaysia SSI 2025 claim scores Medium (three independent secondary-trade sources including a credible law firm alert) but not High, because the official DOSH gazette and PUA 99 text are not directly cited. The Skrine alert is credible but secondary. Fourth, the PwC 2017 engineer-per-million data is nine years stale. Seven claims are High or Medium-high quality (ILO inspector ratio, scale efficiency loss cross-validation with National Board, Singapore MOM regulation, multi-jurisdiction inspection body authorization, Malaysia/Indonesia training provider frameworks). These provide an adequate backbone for the structural arguments. The stage is shippable for qualitative narrative purposes but should carry explicit Low-confidence flags on all dollar-quantified cost claims in PP5.2, PP5.4, and the downtime cost in PP5.1 and PP5.3, pending deep research on three priority items: (1) independent corroboration of retrofit capex and parts lead times, (2) primary DOSH gazette for SSI 2025, and (3) MPOB-based calculation of CPO throughput loss per shutdown hour.
